facts.fact: The article's vendor, StackAdapt, says a generally used marketing funnel has 3 main parts.
facts.quote: there are various ways to define and breakdown the marketing funnel depending on the complexity of your sales cycle, but generally, there are 3 main parts to the funnel

facts.fact: StackAdapt outlines 5 steps for setting up a full-funnel marketing strategy in this article.
facts.quote: We have outlined 5 steps to guide you on how to set up your next full-funnel marketing strategy.

facts.fact: StackAdapt recommends using the 5 W's (who, what, when, where, why) to define the ideal customer profile.
facts.quote: Use the 5 W’s—who, what, when, where, why—to define the ideal customer profile.

facts.fact: StackAdapt describes the upper funnel as the first stage of the buyer's journey, also called the awareness stage, where brands prospect new customers.
facts.quote: Upper funnel is the first stage of the buyer’s journey. In this stage, you are prospecting new customers to introduce them to your brand and offerings.

facts.fact: StackAdapt describes the lower funnel as the conversion stage, where prospects are ready to make a purchase.
facts.quote: Finally, we reach the lower funnel, where prospects have shown interest, they have done their research, and are ready to make a purchase.

facts.fact: StackAdapt says a sales cycle's length and whether there are multiple decision-makers should be considered when choosing where and how to reach an audience.
facts.quote: What is the length of your sales cycle? Are there multiple decision-makers?

facts.fact: StackAdapt says an exclusion audience can be created of users who have completed a conversion so that ad spend is not wasted on them.
facts.quote: This can be done by creating an exclusion audience of users who have completed a conversion or have satisfied a predefined parameter that is important to your business.

facts.fact: The article was published on July 13, 2020.
For an upper-funnel native ad strategy aimed at driving awareness and website visits, the page names CTR as the key native metric to set as a goal.
facts.quote: In this case, the key native metric to set as a goal is CTR.

facts.fact: For a mid-funnel native ad strategy, the page names engagement, measured as time on site, as the key metric to aim for.
facts.quote: the key metric you are aiming for is engagement—time on site.

facts.fact: The page states that the B2B sales cycle is usually longer than B2C because of a multi-step buying process involving multiple decision-makers, and B2B purchases are typically higher-ticket items.
facts.quote: the sales cycle for B2B products or services is usually longer due to the multi-step buying process—involving multiple decision-makers and is typically a higher-ticket item.

facts.fact: The page describes the full-funnel stages as awareness, engagement, consideration, and conversion, and says this concept is the same for B2B and B2C.
